description:
Dopamine Detox | Sitar Music for Mental Reset | 1.5 Hours

If your brain feels overstimulated from scrolling, notifications, and constant input — this is your reset.

90 minutes of slow, contemplative sitar designed to quiet the mental noise and restore your focus. Let your nervous system settle.

What you'll hear:
• Slow Hindustani sitar — meditative phrasing, no sudden shifts
• Soft tabla and tanpura grounding the silence
• Recorded warm and intimate, no electronic processing

Best for:
• Post-work decompression
• Reading or quiet focus
• Reset after heavy screen time
• Anxious or scattered evenings

Press play. Put the phone down. Let your mind empty.
suno_prompt_note: PARKED — user noted Suno prompts not landing well on text-based outputs. Needs separate Suno exploration session. Music quality is the actual experiment variable here per session_findings Finding 3 — must apply CALM rule (avoid: upbeat/uplifting/energetic/forward momentum/not sleepy/never sluggish/driving/propulsive; include: slow/spacious/low register/long pauses/no momentum/breath between notes/restful) regardless of final prompt phrasing.

experiment.hypothesis: Calm Suno prompt fixes the dopamine lane's weak music retention (RRP 0.42 baseline per session_findings_2026-06-26.md Finding 3). Previous Jun 22 Dopamine Boost replica failed (AVP 15.6%, 881 views) — attributed to upbeat music in calm-lane prompt. This ship inverts that: same lane, calm prompt.
experiment.success_criteria: AVD >= 25% AND views >= 10K within 7 days = hypothesis confirmed, lane is music-fixable
experiment.failure_criteria: AVD < 20% AND views < 5K within 7 days = lane structurally weak (low RPM + cannibalized by hero), retire Dopamine angle for future ships
experiment.neutral_zone: AVD 20-25% or views 5-10K = directional, needs second test to confirm
